difficultyRationale: Tests type erasure and the resulting restriction on overloads that differ only in generic type arguments.
prompt: Can one class declare both `void process(List<String> x)` and `void process(List<Integer> x)`?
explanation: No. After type erasure, both parameter types erase to `List`, so the two methods have the same erased signature and cause a name clash.

options.text: Yes, because String and Integer are unrelated types.
options.explanation: Generic type arguments are erased for the method signature used here.

options.text: No, because both methods erase to the same signature.
options.explanation: Both parameterized List types erase to raw List.

options.text: Yes, but only if one method is static.
options.explanation: Static versus instance does not solve the erased-signature clash.

options.text: No, because Java forbids overloading methods named process.
options.explanation: Java permits overloading; the issue is the identical erasure.
